glossary.definition: What the rules said about one request: PERMIT, DENY, or INDETERMINATE (the request had nothing the rules can read). INDETERMINATE is shown as such and is never read as a permit.

A local stand-in for PingOne Authorize. It answers decision requests in the same shape from rules you can edit, so a client can run its normal flow with no tenant. It is a simulation: its verdicts are not PingOne's. The response shapes follow the AI-DEMO2 integration and are UNVERIFIED against PingOne's own documentation.

A guard that refuses every outbound socket, DNS lookup, fetch, UDP send and UDP connect. This app only answers requests; it never calls out. A self-test proves the guard works and a test proves a whole session makes zero attempts.

The token, decisionEndpoints, decision and recentDecisions routes under /pingone, with the environment id in the path accepted as given. A client such as the P1AZ Inspector in Real mode can point at it unchanged. The on-prem PingAuthorize path is also answered. Both shapes are UNVERIFIED against a real PingOne or PingAuthorize.

Puts the session back to a fresh start: rules back to defaults, the decision log cleared, issued tokens ended. The worker credentials are kept, so a client that already holds the secret keeps working.

The editable knobs the Mock engine decides with: the deny limit, the step-up limit, the transaction types that always need consent, the MCP tools that are never allowed and the tools that need a person's approval. Saved rules are a sparse overlay on the defaults; a value set back to its default is dropped.

The named reasons that come back with a verdict. A gate such as step-up, consent or human approval is a PERMIT plus a statement whose code names it (STEP_UP_MFA, HITL_CONSENT), as PingOne's endpoint signals it (UNVERIFIED).

A client_credentials access token a client gets from the mock token endpoint with the mock worker client id and secret. It is Mock-issued, labelled as such, and only good here. Reset ends every token issued so far.

cards.label: Point a client at the mock
cards.description: The base URL and the mock worker credentials, ready to paste into a PingOne-shaped client.

cards.label: How a decision travels
cards.description: Client, token, decision endpoint, rules and verdict as a movable diagram with Simulate.

cards.label: Edit the rules
cards.description: Change the deny limit, the step-up limit and the tool lists. The next decision follows.

cards.label: Send a request and read the verdict
cards.description: Send a transaction or an MCP tool call and see the verdict, the statements and the exact answer.

stories.title: Set the rules
stories.say: Open Rules. Lower the deny limit, add a tool that is never allowed, and save. The next decision follows the change; no restart, no tenant.

stories.title: Try a request
stories.say: On Try, send a transaction or an MCP tool call and read the verdict, the statements and PingOne's answer. A gate such as step-up is a permit plus a statement that names it.

stories.title: Point a client at it
stories.say: Connect shows the base URL and the mock worker credentials. A client gets a token, calls the decision endpoint and its call appears on Decisions marked API next to your own.

stories.title: Start over
stories.say: Reset session restores the default rules, clears the decision log and ends issued tokens. The worker credentials stay, so a client that has the secret still works.
